name: Palmoplantar Keratoderma with Tonotubular Keratin

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Palmoplantar Keratoderma with Tonotubular Keratin

criteria.description: Presence of diffuse or focal thickening of the skin on palms and soles
Histological identification of tonotubular keratin structures in affected skin biopsy
Identification of pathogenic variants in keratin-related genes associated with the condition
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical palmoplantar keratoderma and histopathological confirmation of tonotubular keratin
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory; family history may aid in clinical suspicion.

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing tonotubular keratin filaments under electron microscopy
imaging: Not typically required; imaging may be used to exclude musculoskeletal complications
genetic: Mutations in keratin genes (e.g., KRT1, KRT9) associated with palmoplantar keratoderma variants
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic thickened palmoplantar skin

distinguishingFeatures: Associated with painful keratoderma and transgrediens
Histology does not show tonotubular keratin
Often linked to different inheritance patterns

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin thickening with ulceration
Signs of secondary infection such as fever or purulence
Development of severe pain or functional impairment of hands or feet
